newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia adopts 1997 government spending proposal.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia adopts 1997 government spending proposal.

text.p: Slovenia's government on Monday adopted a 1997 budget proposal, setting government spending at 737.9 billion tolars ($4.4 billion) on income of 710 billion.
"After tough negotiations we managed to adopt a budget that would have a deficit of less than one percent of GDP," deputy prime minister Marjan Podobnik told a news conference.
The government has forecast a four percent growth of GDP this year, while the 1996 GDP reached 1,181.2 billion tolars.
Finance Minister Mitja Gaspari said the deficit would mainly be covered by domestic loans.

He said the government decided to raise the spending plan from its earlier target of 730 billion tolars after it became clear income would be higher than expected on account of purchase taxes, taxes on profits and taxes on salaries.
The parliament is expected to start debating the budget in September but is unlikely to pass it before October.
Currently the government is using a draft budget for the first nine months which was adopted at the end of June.
The opposition last week called for a parliamentary debate on the government's effectiveness, mainly due to its failure to draw up a budget proposal for 1997 earlier.
The government blames the delay on the fact that the coalition was only formed at the end of February after inconclusive November general elections.
The 1996 government spending amounted to 597.5 billion tolars on income of 613.8 billion.
